title: Operator Inkling: taskization pipeline for one-click remediations
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Introduce 'Operator Inkling' — a lightweight suggestion + taskifier that converts contextual diagnostic signals into pre-validated runbook tasks (runlets) for fast operator remediation. The goal is not to fully automate risky fixes, but to reduce cognitive load and time-to-remediate by surfacing a validated, parameterized task that an operator can review and execute with one click. This ticket builds the end-to-end pipeline: suggestion heuristics, runlet template selection, permission checks and audit logging, dry-run & simulation, and a controlled canary rollout in the Console and ops CLI.
background: We frequently observe the same triage steps repeated across incidents: collect logs, tail aggregator, flush worker queue, bump replicas, or rotate cache keys. Current runbooks are long prose; converting those into structured tasks reduces error and speeds MTTR. Previous work on runbook templating exists (ENG-271444, ENG-314572) but focused on authoring. Operator Inkling focuses on generation and safe taskification from live signals and Console context.
acceptance_criteria: Console shows contextual Inkling suggestions for at least 5 common scenarios (worker-saturation, cache-stale, rate-limit spike, model-oom, kv-cache-eviction) with confidence scores
Selecting a suggestion opens a pre-filled runlet with parameters; parameters editable by operator
One-click execute performs dry-run (no state change) then requires explicit confirm to mutate state
All executions produce structured audit entries (actor, params, pre-state snapshot, post-state snapshot) compatible with existing audit export pipeline
Permission gating enforced via RBAC: only users with runlet.execute role can run destructive actions
Telemetry emits inkling.suggested, inkling.accepted, inkling.executed, inkling.reverted with dimensions (scenario, confidence_bucket, region, assignee)
Canary rollout exposes Inkling to 10% of oncall users and logs no false-positive destructive runs in 2 weeks
tasks: Design: UX flows and hint placement in Console (Confluence > Operator Inkling UX v1)
Heuristics: define signature rules + model-classifier fallback for ambiguous contexts
Runlet catalog: map existing runbooks to parameterized templates and author missing templates
Taskizer service: implement suggestion -> runlet compiler API with validation layer
Security: integrate RBAC checks and ensure KMS-encrypted param storage for secrets
Telemetry: add events and dashboards for monitoring suggestion quality and execution safety
CLI: add inkling preview and accept subcommands to opsctl
E2E tests: dry-run regression harness and chaos scenario validation
Rollout: phased canary and rollback playbook
notes: Open questions: do we ship simple rule-based suggestions first, or invest in a small classifier to reduce noise? Trade-offs: classifier reduces spurious suggestions but adds model maintenance and higher latency. Proposed plan: start with deterministic signatures for the five scenarios above, collect telemetry, then iterate with a lightweight binary classifier (logistic) using features from logs and route metadata.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal preview for SRE and Platform Eng (2 weeks) with feature flag
Phase 1: Canary to 10% of oncall users; monitor false accept rate and execution errors (2 weeks)
Phase 2: 50% rollout with UI refinements and telemetry thresholds for auto-disable
Phase 3: GA to all customers with admin toggle and audit export enabled
rollback_plan: Feature flag off: immediate disable of suggestions
Revert service deployment + DB migrations if runlet schema incompatible
Run incident bridge if >3 inadvertent destructive executions in 24h
testing_criteria: Unit tests for Taskizer validation paths and RBAC enforcement
Integration test that simulates Console context and verifies suggestion -> runlet translation
Dry-run E2E that asserts no state change and consistent pre/post snapshots
Chaos test that injects noisy logs to ensure signature resilience
implementation_decisions: Start with deterministic, authorable signatures stored in Git (simple YAML), move to model-backed suggestions in a follow-up
Runlet templates will be stored in the existing runlet-catalog service (backwards compatible API)
Audit entries use existing structured-event schema to avoid new consumers needing adapters
